Subject: SIG follow-up: Encryption, KMS/HSM, and rotation evidence

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for sending the SIG questionnaire. Our InfoSec team has a couple of follow-ups specific to encryption and key management before we close the review:

1) In-transit encryption: please confirm TLS versions supported for public API endpoints and provide the current cipher-suite matrix.

2) At-rest encryption: confirm which data classes are encrypted at rest (tokens, user content, logs, backups) and the encryption algorithms used.

3) KMS/HSM: clarify whether keys are managed in a cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS / GCP KMS) or a customer-managed HSM. If using a cloud KMS, provide an architecture diagram showing separation of control plane, data plane, and any external key access patterns. If using HSM, describe the vendor and FIPS validation.

4) Key rotation: provide your key rotation policy (frequency, automated/manual, emergency rotation process) and an example audit entry showing a recent rotation (redact identifying values).

5) Dual control / separation of duties: who can perform key operations (create/rotate/delete) and what approvals are required?

We need these items for closure by EOD Friday if possible. Attachments preferred as PDFs or links to shared Drive.

Thanks,
Jane

Marissa —

Draft answers and artifacts are attached to the shared Drive (link below). Summary:

- TLS / In-transit: Public API endpoints terminate TLS 1.2 and 1.3 (TLS 1.3 preferred). Current cipher-suite matrix included in tls_cipher-suite-matrix.csv (we disable known weak ciphers; ECDHE + AES-GCM/ChaCha20 are default).

- At-rest: Customer content (input/output text), embeddings, model weights cache, and backups are encrypted at rest. We use AES-256-GCM for object storage and disk encryption on nodes. Database (metadata) uses TDE where supported. Logs that contain PII are routed to a secured bucket and encrypted; ephemeral request logs are rotated/retained per retention policy.

- KMS/HSM architecture: Hosted mode uses customer-tenant keys stored in the cloud provider KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) per-region; Redwood's control plane stores only encrypted key references. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via BYOK + HSM import. Attached: redwood_kms_architecture_v1.pdf (redacted diagram showing control/data plane separation).

- Key rotation: We rotate root/management keys on a scheduled cadence: service keys rotate once every 12 months by default; customer master keys are scheduled per-customer (recommended 90 days) but can be configured. Rotation is automated via KeyOps with an orchestrated rewrap flow; emergency rotation is handled via our Security On-Call with coordinated cache flush and fallback model variants. Document: key_rotation_policy_2024-11.pdf.

- Separation of duties: Key creation/rotation requests originate from the KeyOps service; only principals in the KeyOps role (internal security engineers) plus the relevant customer admins can trigger create/rotate. Delete requires multi-person approval (two internal approvers) and an approval ticket.

- Audit sample: Included a sanitized rotation log entry (timestamps, actor role, operation, key alias) in the Drive.

Drive (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/security/sig/evidence-pack-ACME-20250320

I attached small stubs here as well (PDFs + CSV) for quick review. Let me know if you'd like me to redact further before sending externally.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Jane —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find our responses and supporting artifacts below — attached are PDF stubs and a cipher matrix for quick review; full redacted evidence is available on the shared Drive link if you need additional context (link below).

1) In-transit encryption
- Supported TLS versions: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 (TLS 1.3 preferred).
- Cipher suite guidance: we prefer ECDHE-based suites with AEAD (see tls_cipher-suite-matrix.csv). We disable RC4, 3DES, and known weak suites.

2) At-rest encryption
- Data classes encrypted: customer inputs/outputs, embeddings, model caching layers, snapshots/backups, and metadata stores (where supported via TDE). Encryption algorithm: AES-256-GCM for object and block storage; database TDE uses AES-256 variants. Logs containing sensitive data are encrypted at rest and subject to our log retention policy.

3) KMS/HSM architecture
- Hosted: keys are managed in the cloud KMS (per-region AWS KMS or GCP KMS). Our control plane stores only encrypted key references and never stores raw key material. See redwood_kms_architecture_v1.pdf (attached redacted diagram).
- Dedicated/Private: customer-managed keys are supported via BYOK; HSM imports (FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated vendors) are available on request.

4) Key rotation
- Policy summary: service-managed keys rotate annually; customer CMKs recommended rotation cadence is configurable (default 90 days). Rotation is automated using our KeyOps orchestration that performs rewraps and orchestrates cache invalidation. Emergency rotation is run through Incident Response with post-rotation verification steps documented in key_rotation_policy_2024-11.pdf (attached).

5) Dual control / separation of duties
- Only principals with the KeyOps role and customer admins can perform create/rotate operations. Deletes require two internal approvers and a ticket in our change management system. All key operations are logged and available for audit.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_kms_architecture_v1.pdf, key_rotation_policy_2024-11.pdf, tls_cipher-suite-matrix.csv

Drive (redacted evidence): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/security/sig/evidence-pack-ACME-20250320

If you'd like, we can schedule a short call with Karthik and our infra security lead to walk through the architecture diagram and rotation workflow.

Thanks — looking forward to closure.

Best,
